threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'pram' instead of a 'buggy.' Locals know it's all about the 'add to cart' on social media, not the high street.
Caught the N159 last night; a guy in a tutu was arguing with a pigeon over a chip. The pigeon won, and he just shrugged it off. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids building a makeshift skate ramp with just pallets and a tarp in the park. Pure Neukölln creativity.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it's normal to get a döner at 3 AM and hear a spontaneous jam session in the park. Only here do late-night snacks come with live music.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their ability to navigate BART delays. Outsiders still panic when the train stalls, while we just shrug and look for tacos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tux waiting for the 31 while sipping a cocktail. Only in SF do you get dressed up to ride Muni at 5 PM.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm lies in its tiny peixateries and the neighbors’ gossip over shoulder-high fences.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them easily by how they still ask for a menú del dia at dinner time, oblivious to the locals only craving tapas after eight.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused at the bus stop when the driver waves you past. Locals know you just hop on anywhere, mate.
Caught a night bus from Brixton the other week; two blokes started arguing over who had the loudest Spotify playlist. It was like a mini rave in the back.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted an old man feeding pigeons outside the Türkischer Markt, I realized this place breathes culture, history, and a touch of chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you watch a techno DJ mix while waiting for your bus at 6 AM on a Sunday. It's all part of the rich, chaotic tapestry here.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone's local when they can name all the taco trucks and still find a new one that just popped up last week.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading commuters with an accordion while the 47 sat idle at Jones. For a moment, it felt like a scene straight out of a movie.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists keep asking where the 'real Gràcia' is, completely missing the fact that the vibe changes every hour with locals just living their lives.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for directions to places like Parc Güell while clutching a map instead of using their phones. You spot them in the same cafes every day.
